- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias, especially after sharp drops.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >75), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply a “cool-down” correction to forecast.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; align forecast with sentiment change lag.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon after extreme moves; if forecast is >75 or <65, apply a 1–2 day mean-reversion adjustment.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “0.33” in 3+ consecutive days, model tends to drift toward 70–72; cap forecast near 72 unless sentiment flips.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates when sentiment is “neutral” or “negative” — reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment <0.50 for 5+ days.
